title: Measuring Length and Height
keyIdea: Length is how long something is along a line. Height is how tall it stands. To compare fairly, line up the starting ends. Measure with the same non-standard unit end to end — no gaps or overlaps.
familyTip: Put two pencils side by side. Ask: 'Did we line up the starts?' Then measure a book with cubes or paper clips: 'How many cubes long?'

visual.caption: Fair measure or unfair? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: starts lined up, cubes end to end
one start line for both objects
mixing huge and tiny units in one count

lab.caption: Flagship lab: line up starts, compare longer and taller, measure with cubes, and catch unfair-measure slips.

kid: Length means how long something is from end to end. Height means how tall it stands.
Before you compare, line up the starting ends. Looking only at the far ends is not fair.
You can measure with cubes or hand spans. Use the same unit each time, touching end to end with no gaps.
Longer is not the same word as taller. A long ribbon can lie flat. A tall tower stands up.
adult: Year 1 measure: compare, describe and solve practical problems for lengths and heights; measure with non-standard units. Words: length, height, longer, shorter, taller, unit, line up, gap, overlap.
Common mistakes: comparing only far ends; leaving gaps between units; mixing unit sizes; swapping taller with longer; thinking heavier means longer.
In the lab your child lines up starts, picks longer vs shorter and taller vs shorter, lays cubes along a bar, fixes an unfair start/unit choice, then faces challenge traps for those slips.

practice.prompt: Before comparing two lengths, you should…
choices: only look at the far ends
practice.hint: Fair compares share the same start.
practice.explain: Line up the starts first. Comparing only far ends (or flipping) makes the compare unfair.

choices: is always longer flat on the table
practice.hint: Height is about how high something stands.
practice.explain: Taller is height. Longer is along a line. Weight is a different attribute.

practice.prompt: A ribbon is {n} cubes long. Another is {k} cubes long. How much longer is the first?
practice.hint: Subtract the shorter cube count from the longer.

practice.prompt: You place {n} cubes end to end. How many units long is the object?
practice.hint: Each cube is one unit when they touch with no gaps.
Same unit, no gaps or overlaps.
practice.explain: Equal cubes must touch end to end. Gaps or mixed sizes make the count unfair.

choices: how long something is along a line
pool.hint: Think end to end in space.
pool.explain: Length measures distance along a line — not sound or mass.

pool.hint: Starts must line up before any fair compare.
pool.explain: If starts do not line up, the compare is unfair. It does not change mass.

pool.hint: Up from the ground or base.
pool.explain: Height is standing tall. Width and colour are different.

choices: so the count means the same each time
so you can skip lining up
pool.explain: Same-size units make counts comparable. Looks and skipping line-up are not the goal.

pool.prompt: Tower A is {n} cubes tall. Tower B is {k} cubes tall. How many cubes taller is A?
You need {n} cubes to measure a book. How many cubes do you need?
pool.hint: Use one cube per unit along the length.
pool.explain: You need {n} cubes for a fair end-to-end measure.

pool.hint: Longer means more distance along a line.
pool.explain: Longer covers more end to end. Taller is height; colour is unrelated.

pool.prompt: Mixing huge and tiny units in one count is…
pool.hint: Every unit in one measure must be the same size.
pool.explain: Mixed unit sizes make the number meaningless. Keep units the same.
